title: Arc Length and Sector Area (Degrees and Radians)
seo_title: Arc Length and Sector Area Worksheet with Radians (Geometry, G-C.B.5) | 100 Questions with Answers
standard_text: Derive using similarity the fact that the length of the arc intercepted by an angle is proportional to the radius, and define the radian measure of the angle as the constant of proportionality; derive the formula for the area of a sector.
meta_desc: Free Geometry worksheet on arc length and sector area in degrees and radians: answers in terms of π, perimeter of a sector, and word problems. 100 questions with answers.
key_big: A sector is θ/360 of the whole circle.
key_sub: Arc length = θ/360 × 2πr. In radians, s = rθ and the area is ½r²θ.
body_html:
How it works

A sector is a slice of a circle between two radii. Its curved edge is an arc. If the angle at the center is θ, the sector is the fraction θ/360 of the whole circle.

Arc length = θ/360 × 2πr. Sector area = θ/360 × πr². The perimeter of a sector is the arc length plus two radii.

In radians (π radians = 180°), the arc length is s = rθ and the sector area is ½r²θ. The radian measure of an angle is the arc length divided by the radius.

Example

Arc length: θ = 60°, r = 9 cm.

60/360 = ⅙.

⅙ × 2π × 9 = 3π.

Answer: 9.4 cm

Example

Sector area: θ = 60°, r = 9 cm.

⅙ × π × 81 = 13.5π.

Answer: 42.4 cm²

Example

Perimeter of that sector.

9.4 + 9 + 9.

Answer: 27.4 cm

Common mistakes

  • Using 2πr for the area or πr² for the arc.
  • Forgetting to multiply by θ/360.
  • Forgetting the two straight edges when finding the perimeter.
  • Using the diameter as the radius.
  • Mixing degree and radian formulas. With radians, s = rθ and the area is ½r²θ.

faq.q: How do I find the arc length?
faq.a: Multiply the circumference 2πr by the fraction θ/360. In radians, the arc length is simply s = rθ.

faq.q: How do I find the area of a sector?
faq.a: Multiply the circle's area πr² by θ/360. In radians, the area is ½r²θ.

faq.q: How do you convert degrees to radians?
faq.a: Multiply by π/180. For example, 60° × π/180 = π/3 radians.

faq.q: What is the perimeter of a sector?
faq.a: The arc length plus the two radii.

items.q: Convert π2 radians to degrees.
items.e: π radians = 180°, so π2 = 90°.

items.q: A sector has radius 18 cm and central angle π2 radians. Find the arc length in terms of π.
items.e: In radians, arc length s = rθ = 18 × π2 = 9π cm.

items.q: A sector of radius 10 cm has area 252π cm². What is the angle of the sector?
items.e: θ/360 × 100π = 252π cm². So θ = 360 × 252 ÷ 100 = 45°.

items.q: A sector of radius 9 cm has area 272π cm². What is the angle of the sector?
items.e: θ/360 × 81π = 272π cm². So θ = 360 × 272 ÷ 81 = 60°.

items.q: A pizza has radius 15 cm. It is cut into 8 equal slices. What is the area of one slice, to 1 decimal place?
items.e: Each slice is a 45° sector: 1/8 × π × 15² = 88.4 cm².

items.q: A clock's minute hand is 10 cm long. How far does its tip travel in 15 minutes, to 1 decimal place?
items.e: 15 minutes is a quarter turn: ¼ × 2π × 10 = 15.7 cm.

items.q: A clock's minute hand is 12 cm long. What area does it sweep in 20 minutes, in terms of π?
items.e: 20 minutes is ⅓ of a turn: ⅓ × π × 12² = 48π cm².

items.e: Curved part: ½ × π × 10 = 15.7 cm. Add the diameter: 15.7 + 10 = 25.7 cm.

Two sectors have the same radius. One has angle 60° and the other 120°. How do their areas compare?
c: The 120° sector is twice as big
The 120° sector is four times as big
items.e: Area is proportional to the angle, so doubling the angle doubles the area: the 120° sector is twice as big.

items.q: If the radius of a sector doubles and the angle stays the same, what happens to its area?
items.e: Area uses r², and 2² = 4, so it is multiplied by 4.

items.q: If the radius of a sector doubles and the angle stays the same, what happens to its arc length?
items.e: Arc length is proportional to r, so it doubles.

items.e: The circumference is 18π, so the sector is ⅓ of the circle. Area = ⅓ × 81π = 27π cm².

items.q: Which formula gives the arc length of a sector with angle θ?
items.e: Arc length is the fraction θ/360 of the circumference: θ/360 × 2πr.

items.q: Which formula gives the area of a sector with angle θ?
items.e: Sector area is the fraction θ/360 of the circle's area: θ/360 × πr².
